title: Wealth Tax Debate, Midterm Investing, AI Anxiety
summary: Bloomberg Money takes the pulse of your financial life, powered by the reporting of our global newsroom. Today's guests: Whitney Tilson, Stansberry Research Editor, and Stephanie Guild, Robinhood CIO. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Andrew Brandt on MLB Salary Cap Fight as World Series Begins
summary: Andrew Brandt says the Brewers and Rays reaching the World Series—despite ranking 19th and 26th in payroll, respectively—shows how strong management, scouting and player development can compete with high spending. He calls the matchup evidence for the players’ union that success is possible without a salary cap, while cautioning that owners may dismiss it as an unsustainable exception: smaller-market teams have little margin for error and can lose players to wealthier clubs in free agency. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: How Valterra's Forging the Future of Platinum | Chief Financial Officer
summary: Chief Financial Officers now play a critical role in shaping corporate strategy and positioning organizations to meet future challenges. This episode profiles Valterra Platinum CFO Sayurie Naidoo, who leads the world's largest company producing platinum group metals. One year after its demerger from Anglo American, the South African firm is looking ahead to develop new markets for PGMs as the adoption of battery electric vehicles threatens their primary area of demand. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: 'Notes on Being a Man', 'The Invisible Hand'
summary: Bloomberg's Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene discuss their must-read book on this week's edition of "Bloomberg Money." title: US Family Annual Healthcare Plan Now Costs More Than $28K
summary: Bloomberg's John Tozzi joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: San Diego to Leave Muni Bond Group After SEC Oversight Concerns
summary: The city of San Diego said it plans to withdraw from a group that helps issue and manage billions of dollars in municipal bonds after federal regulators raised concerns about the organization’s oversight.

title: Chipmakers Post Longest Weekly Drop Since November
summary: A resurgence in oil prices dragged down stocks and bonds, stoking concerns about inflation just days ahead of the Federal Reserve decision on interest rates. Brent crude settled near $117 as a flare-up in Middle East violence threatened supplies. Most S&P 500 firms fell even as selling pressure on tech shares abated. A gauge of chipmakers edged up, but posted its longest weekly drop since November. The Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 1.2%. Treasuries relinquished a portion of the previous session’s rally. Co-Host of Odd Lots, Joe Weisenthal says it's important to the US Economy that tech companies fire on all cylinders.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Hedge Funds Are Record Short Natural Gas on Mild Winter Outlook
summary: Hedge-fund managers have amassed a record short position in US natural gas on expectations for an unusually mild northern winter that points to anemic demand for the furnace and power-plant fuel.

title: Oncologists Cheer Melanoma Data
summary:
Leaked data from Moderna and Merck's highly anticipated melanoma vaccine trial has led to a rare disconnect between doctors, who celebrated the result, and Wall Street, which sold off the stocks.
Normally results of such pivotal drug studies are binary, with doctors, patients and investors all learning whether a novel medicine will make a meaningful difference in people’s lives and forming the same conclusion. Instead, as reports leaked out on social media about the findings of the melanoma shot — days before the carefully scripted presentation planned for thousands of oncologists gathered in Madrid for the European Society for Medical Oncology meeting — realities diverged.  Madison Muller, Bloomberg News Healthcare Reporter, reports.   (Source: Bloomberg)
